request.spec:
A hold now has a from-date (default the sheet's today) and an optional to-date, and a person may
have several holds over time. Only a person's OPEN claims dated within a hold are left out of the
live totals; their other open claims count, and a claim bound by a statement stays in the totals
whatever its date. Show hold yes/no as whether the person has any hold. Holding writes
PERSON_HELD name=<name> from=<date>; releasing is no longer a separate action (a hold ends on
its to-date).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A hold now has a from-date (default the sheet's today) and an optional to-date, and a person may
have several holds over time. Only a person's OPEN claims dated within a hold are left out of the
live totals; their other open claims count, and a claim bound by a statement stays in the totals
whatever its date. Show hold yes/no as whether the person has any hold. Holding writes
PERSON_HELD name=<name> from=<date>; releasing is no longer a separate action (a hold ends on
its to-date).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Holds now have a from-date and an optional to-date, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**What changed**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V33__person_hold_interval.sql`, adds a `person_hold` table holding a from-date and an optional to-date. A person can have any number of rows in it. It replaces the old `held` column, which the migration drops.
- **Server:**
  - A person's holds are kept in the new `PersonHold` class.
  - Holding a person writes `PERSON_HELD name=<name> from=<date>`. A blank from-date takes the sheet's today. The release action and the `PERSON_RELEASED` record are gone.
  - The rule for what counts in the live totals is in `RollupService.countsLive`. The statement and period totals already go through it, so all three follow the new rule.
- **Front end:** each person's row has Hold from / Hold to fields and a Hold button, and lists their holds (`person-hold-line`). The row works out its totals in the browser using the same rule as the server. "On hold" shows yes if the person has any hold at all, even one whose to-date has passed.

**Decisions to check**
- **Hold dates:** both ends count as inside the hold, and a blank to-date means the hold never ends.
- **Refused holds:** the app refuses a hold whose to-date is before its from-date, or one that exactly repeats a hold the person already has. Both show `person-error`.
- **PENDING claims:** the app already treats a PENDING claim as not bound by a statement, so a PENDING claim dated within a hold is left out even if it was stated. The request only says "OPEN claims"; if PENDING claims should behave differently here, it's a one-line change in each of the two places the rule lives.
- **Existing held people:** people on hold before this change get a hold from `0001-01-01` with no end. That keeps their old behaviour of all open claims being left out.
